fields.name: LOCK
fields.why: pll_init() spins `while (!(pll->cs & PLL_CS_LOCK_BITS)) tight_loop_contents();` (src/rp2_common/hardware_pll/pll.c:63, fetched this session -- VERIFIED, quoted) immediately after `hw_clear_bits(&pll->pwr, PLL_PWR_PD_BITS | PLL_PWR_VCOPD_BITS)` (pll.c:57-60). LOCK's real hardware condition is PD==0 AND VCOPD==0 (PWR resets to 0x2d, i.e. fully powered down, per PWR's why-note below). UPDATED 2026-08-24: this is now the doc's own motivating case for multi-source `follows` (list + `op: "and"`, `when` applying uniformly) -- stm-soc adopted the grammar with this exact field written in verbatim. The prior single-field approximation (follows:"PWR.PD" alone) was noted as behaviourally indistinguishable for stock pico-sdk, since pll_init's hw_clear_bits call clears PD and VCOPD together in one write -- that note is preserved here as it explains why the approximation was safe, not because it is still the model.

fields.name: BYPASS
fields.why: Not written by pll_init()'s stock path -- included for completeness only.

fields.name: REFDIV
fields.why: pll_init() writes `pll->cs = refdiv` (pll.c:53) before powering up the VCO.

registers.name: PWR
registers.why_reset_value: 0x2d = PD=1, DSMPD=1, POSTDIVPD=1, VCOPD=1 -- the PLL comes up FULLY POWERED DOWN. pll_init() must explicitly clear PD+VCOPD before LOCK can ever assert; a model that defaults PWR to all-zero would let LOCK go true without firmware ever powering the PLL, masking a real firmware-correctness class.

fields.name: VCOPD
fields.source: pll.h:62-70 (pico-sdk). VERIFIED. See CS.LOCK's why-note for the two-field-AND caveat this field is part of.

fields.name: POSTDIVPD
fields.why: pll_init() clears this LAST (pll.c:69), after LOCK is already confirmed -- the post divider is deliberately held powered-down until the VCO is locked.

fields.name: DSMPD
fields.why: 'Nothing is achieved by setting this low' -- this PLL has no usable fractional mode; correct firmware leaves it at reset value.

fields.name: FBDIV_INT
fields.why: pll_init() writes this (pll.c:54) before powering up the VCO, and its own early-out check (pll.c:42-48) reads it back to skip re-init if the PLL is already correctly configured -- must round-trip a plain write/read independent of LOCK's ready-follows behaviour.
fields.source: pll.h:100-109 (pico-sdk). VERIFIED. 'this PLL does not support fractional division'.

fields.name: POSTDIV2
fields.why: pll_init() writes both dividers together AFTER LOCK is confirmed (pll.c:63-66) -- the post-divider write is not gated by LOCK's condition, it happens once LOCK is already true.

spin_targets: CS.LOCK -- second boot-blocking spin after XOSC.STATUS.STABLE, for both PLL_SYS and PLL_USB instances.
